Verified without a paid turn on `claude` 2.1.251 — the version `PROVEN_CLAUDE_VERSION` names — by three offline reads: `claude --help` says `--model` takes "an alias for the latest model (e.g. 'fable', 'opus', or 'sonnet') or a model's full name (e.g. 'claude-fable-5')"; the baked model catalog inside the binary reads `fable:{default:"claude-fable-5"}`, `latest_per_family:{fable:"claude-fable-5",…}`, `best:"fable"`, with an empty `alias_migration`; and the Vertex region table pairs `claude-fable-5` with `VERTEX_REGION_CLAUDE_FABLE_5`. A grep for `claude-fable-5-1` and "Fable 5.1" over all 345 288 strings of the binary returns nothing. A successor exists in the world — Anthropic has announced Claude Fable 5.1, and Cursor lists `claude-fable-5-1-*` ids — but the binary this driver proves cannot start it, so it is not rated here; this ladder moves when `PROVEN_CLAUDE_VERSION` does. quality: SWE-bench Verified 95.0 %, second of the six rated models banded on that benchmark, so the top fifth — band 5. The same leaderboard puts claude-opus-5 one point above it at 96.0 %, which is the whole distance between bands 5 and 5 here and is the field-size fragility recorded in the finding under this task. This model also carries Terminal-Bench 2.1 figures — 83.8 % on Claude Code and 80.4 % on Terminus 2 — and they are not the basis of any rating here, because SWE-bench Verified comes first in the ADR-004 preference order. They are recorded because the hypotheses on other harnesses are anchored on the 83.8 %, which is the figure measured on Claude Code, the harness this catalog runs this model on. speed: a hypothesis. Cursor's own variant of Grok 4.6, in the `auto` pool. The base row is `-high`, which the listing displays as plain "Cursor Grok 4.6" with no level word — the family's headline id — while `-low`, `-medium` and `-xhigh` carry theirs. There IS a published Terminal-Bench 2.1 figure of 88.4 % for **xAI's Grok 4.6**, and it is not a figure for this model: ADR-004 asks for a figure for "that exact model", the Terminal-bench leaderboard scores the model and its agent harness together, and the one harness-labelled Grok row on it is Grok 4.5 on Cursor CLI at 79.3 % — nine points below the harness-free number. Band 4 on this reasoning: 88.4 % would sit between gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-5.5, and the lower of the two bands is taken because a harness-specific variant is not the vendor's measured configuration. OpenAI does not report SWE-bench Verified for the 5.6 family at all, and this model is absent from the SWE-bench Verified leaderboard that bands the six rated Claude, Kimi, Gemini and GLM rows. The fallback the ADR names is Terminal-bench, and Terminal-bench 2.1 does not hold five rated models on any one agent harness: the figures found are 88.8 % single-agent and 85.77 % on the Vals AI harness for this model, against claude-fable-5 at 83.8 % on Claude Code and 83.4 % elsewhere. It is the strongest thing Codex will start, and the reviewer floor of ADR-004 is met by judgement, not by a rank — which the table says out loud so the owner can overrule it. speed: 90 tokens/s, sixth of nine — band 3. The figure was measured at max, not at this row's medium base; the ladder below therefore reads the throughput of a deeper level than it describes, and that is recorded rather than corrected. quotaCost: $5 in / $30 out, joint second-dearest of thirteen — band 5. Because the base row is already at the ceiling, every step up this ladder clamps to 5 and the cost column is flat from medium to ultra; that flattening is the ADR clamp, and it is filed as a finding under this task. `ultra` is a real level of this model in `model/list` and reaches the driver (EFFORT_LEVELS in lib/driver-codex.js).
